subject: mathematics
question_text: Show that the determinant with rows (a−b, b−c, c−a), (b−c, c−a, a−b) and (c−a, a−b, b−c) is 0.

recall_prompt: Say how you would show this determinant is zero — name the operation you use.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Add all three columns into C₁
steps.margin_note: First mark. Look along any row before starting: the entries are (a−b), (b−c) and (c−a), and those three add to zero. That is what makes this operation worth doing.
steps.memory_tip: The three entries of every row add to zero, so adding all three columns empties the first one.
lines: Let Δ be the given determinant:

lines.text: \Delta = \begin{vmatrix} a-b & b-c & c-a \\ b-c & c-a & a-b \\ c-a & a-b & b-c \end{vmatrix}

lines: In every row the three entries add to

recall.must_convey: That C₁ → C₁ + C₂ + C₃ is applied, and that each row total is (a−b)+(b−c)+(c−a) = 0.
accept: add column two and column three into column one
apply C one goes to C one plus C two plus C three
every row adds to zero because a minus b plus b minus c plus c minus a is zero
moodu columns kalipithe prathi row zero avutundi
the sum along each row is zero so add the columns together
heard_as: C one plus C two plus C three

steps.why: Adding one column to another leaves the value of a determinant unchanged, so C₁ → C₁ + C₂ + C₃ is allowed and costs nothing.
common_mistakes: Expanding the 3×3 determinant term by term instead of using the column operation.
Thinking that adding columns changes the value of the determinant.

steps.label: Read off the value
steps.margin_note: Second mark. A determinant with one whole column of zeros is zero — expand along that column and every term carries a factor 0.
steps.memory_tip: A determinant with a full row or column of zeros is 0.
lines: So C₁ becomes a column of zeros:

lines.text: \Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 0 & b-c & c-a \\ 0 & c-a & a-b \\ 0 & a-b & b-c \end{vmatrix}

lines: A determinant with a zero column is 0.

recall.must_convey: That the first column becomes all zeros, and that a determinant with a zero column equals 0.
accept: the first column becomes all zeros so the determinant is zero
a determinant with a zero column is zero
after the operation column one is zero zero zero, hence delta is zero
first column antha zero avutundi kabatti determinant zero

steps.why: Expanding along the zero column gives 0 times a cofactor three times over, so the value is 0 for every a, b and c.
common_mistakes: Writing 'hence proved' without naming the zero column.
Deleting the zero column and expanding the 3×2 block that is left.
